title: Ways of speaking
about: Collocations for talking to people: making a speech and telling jokes, raising or changing the subject, dropping a hint, striking up a conversation, telling the truth or a lie and apologising profusely.

parts.title: Common mistakes
parts.note: Мову, якою володієш, англійською speak, а не talk: I speak Arabic, Can you speak French? Talk — розмовляти з кимось або про щось (talk to sb, talk about sth). Say — сказати якісь слова (say something to sb), tell — розповісти, повідомити комусь (tell sb sth). Саме з tell кажуть tell a story, tell a joke, tell the truth, tell a lie. У таблиці — найчастіші пастки цього юніту.

items.pattern: make / give a speech (at an event / about sth) · formal: deliver a speech · a wedding / birthday / welcome speech
items.meaning: stand up and talk formally to a group of people at an event
items.example: At his retirement party, Grandad **made a speech** and thanked everyone by name.
more: The head teacher **gave a speech** about kindness on the last day of term.
I hate **making speeches**, so at my fiftieth I just said, 'Thanks for coming. Enjoy the food!'
items.watchOut: «Виголосити промову» — make / give a speech, а не say a speech і не hold a speech (калька). Speech — промова; мова як система (англійська, українська) — language.

items.pattern: get / come (straight) to the point · Get to the point! · stick to the point
items.meaning: start talking about the most important thing without wasting time on other things
items.uk: перейти до суті, говорити по суті
items.example: Stop talking about the weather and **get to the point**: why did you really call?
more: The estate agent **came straight to the point**: the flat had already been sold.
I'll **get to the point**: we need someone to look after the dog this weekend.
items.watchOut: «Перейти до суті» — get / come to the point; калька pass to the point не працює. Point тут — суть, головне, а не «пункт» чи «крапка». «Не відходь від теми» — stick to the point.

items.pattern: tell (sb) a story / stories (about sb/sth) · tell a funny / true / bedtime story
items.meaning: describe events, real or invented, to someone in an interesting way
items.example: Grandma loves **telling stories** about her childhood in the village.
more: Dad **told** the kids **a story** about a dragon who was afraid of the dark.
My neighbour **told** me **a story** about her cat getting stuck on the roof.
items.watchOut: Історію розповідають — tell a story, а не say a story чи talk a story. Історія як розповідь — story, а history — це наука або минуле країни. Людина стоїть одразу після tell, без to: tell the children a story.

items.pattern: give sb your word (that… / to do sth) · You have my word. · keep / break your word
items.meaning: promise someone very seriously that you will or won't do something
items.example: I **give you my word** that I'll pay you back by Friday.
more: She **gave me her word** that she'd water the plants while I was away.
He **gave his word** and then broke it, so I don't trust him any more.
items.watchOut: «Даю слово» — I give you my word, обов'язково з my / your / his: не give a word і не give the word (give the word — «дати команду, сигнал»: Just give the word and we'll start). Дотримати слова — keep your word, порушити — break your word.

items.pattern: crack / tell a joke / jokes · crack is informal · make jokes (about sb/sth)
items.meaning: say funny things or short funny stories to make people laugh
items.example: Our tour guide kept **cracking jokes**, so the long bus ride went quickly.
more: My little brother loves **telling jokes**, but he always forgets the ending.
Dad **cracked a joke** about the burnt potatoes, and everyone relaxed.
items.watchOut: «Розповідати анекдоти» — tell jokes, а не say jokes чи speak jokes. Crack jokes — розмовне «сипати жартами». Англійське anecdote — кумедна чи цікава історія з життя, а не анекдот.

items.pattern: wish sb (good) luck (with / in sth) · Wish me luck! · I wish you the best of luck.
items.meaning: say that you hope someone will be successful
items.example: My exam starts at nine. **Wish me luck**!
more: We all **wished her luck** before her driving test.
Everyone at work signed a card **wishing** her **luck** with the move to Spain.
items.watchOut: «Бажаю удачі» — I wish you luck або просто Good luck! Не want you luck: want — «хотіти». Людина стоїть одразу після wish: wish your sister luck.

items.pattern: have a brief / quick / short chat (with sb) (about sth) · have a chat
items.meaning: talk with someone in a friendly, informal way for a short time
items.example: I **had a brief chat** with the surgeon before the operation, and she put my mind at rest.
more: Let's **have a quick chat** over coffee before the others arrive.
The coach **had a short chat** with each player after the match.
items.watchOut: Chat — дружня неформальна розмова, а не лише онлайн-чат. «Коротко поговорити» — have a brief / quick chat, а не make a chat. Brief /briːf/ — «короткий».

items.pattern: have a word with sb (about sth) · have a quick / brief word · Can I have a word?
items.meaning: talk to someone for a short time, often in private, about something specific, often a problem
items.uk: поговорити з кимось (коротко, часто про проблему), перекинутися словом
items.example: Could I **have a quick word** with you about Saturday's barbecue?
more: Leave it to me. I'll **have a word with** the manager about the cold food.
The police officer **had a word with** the boys about riding their bikes on the pavement.
items.watchOut: Have a word with sb — не «сказати одне слово», а коротко поговорити, часто щоб розв'язати проблему чи зробити зауваження: I'll have a word with him. Не say a word with sb. А have words with sb (у множині) — посваритися.

items.pattern: a delicate / sensitive subject · a delicate matter / question / situation
items.meaning: a topic you must talk about carefully because it may upset or embarrass people
items.example: Money is a **delicate subject** in our family, so nobody mentions Grandad's will.
more: Her weight is a **delicate subject**, so please don't comment on it.
Ask him about the divorce gently: it's still a **delicate subject**.
items.watchOut: «Тонка, делікатна тема» — a delicate / sensitive subject, а не a thin subject чи a subtle subject. Тема розмови — subject або topic; theme — радше тема книжки, фільму чи свята (a pirate theme).

items.pattern: a lengthy / long discussion (about / on sth) · have a lengthy discussion
items.meaning: a discussion that goes on for a long time, often longer than necessary
items.example: After a **lengthy discussion**, we agreed to spend Christmas at my sister's.
more: Buying the house took ten minutes, but choosing the paint needed a **lengthy discussion**.
The club had a **lengthy discussion** about raising the price of membership.
items.watchOut: «Довге обговорення» — a lengthy / long discussion, а не a large discussion: large — про розмір, а не про час. Lengthy часто означає «задовгий»: a lengthy wait, a lengthy letter.

items.pattern: raise / bring up the subject (of sth) · raise a question / a problem / an issue
items.meaning: start talking about a particular topic
items.example: I didn't want to **raise the subject** of money at dinner, but someone had to.
more: My sister finally **raised the subject** of the wedding costs with her parents.
She **brought up the subject** of moving house while we were washing up.
items.watchOut: Порушити тему — raise (raised, raised): у нього є додаток, raise the subject. Не плутай із rise (rose, risen) — «підніматися» саме по собі, без додатка: prices rise. Не lift the subject: lift — піднімати фізично.

items.pattern: (speak / say sth / tell sb sth) off the record · strictly off the record · opposite: on the record
items.meaning: said privately and not meant to be repeated or reported
items.uk: неофіційно, між нами, не для протоколу
items.example: **Off the record**, the manager told me the shop will close next year.
more: I'm telling you this **off the record**, so please don't mention it at school.
**Strictly off the record**, the doctor said the clinic is short of nurses.
items.watchOut: «Не для протоколу» — off the record, а не not for the protocol чи out of the record. Англійське protocol — зазвичай правила етикету чи процедура, а протокол зборів — the minutes.

items.pattern: give (sb) instructions (on / about sth / to do sth) · follow instructions · clear / detailed instructions
items.meaning: tell someone exactly what to do or how to do something
items.example: The nurse **gave me instructions** on how to change the bandage.
more: The coach **gave** each player clear **instructions** before the second half.
Our driving instructor **gives** very clear **instructions**, so I never panic.
items.watchOut: «Давати інструкції» — give instructions, а не make instructions чи say instructions. Виконувати — follow instructions. Інструкція до техніки — the instructions (у множині) або the manual.

items.pattern: challenge sb (directly) (about / on sth) · challenge sb's decision / story
items.meaning: openly question what someone has said or done and ask them to explain it
items.uk: прямо висловити комусь претензію, напряму поставити під сумнів чиїсь слова чи дії
items.example: When I **challenged him directly** about the broken window, he admitted it was his ball.
more: My sister isn't afraid to **challenge** people **directly** when they jump the queue.
My daughter **challenged** her teacher **directly** about the low mark, and he agreed to look at it again.
items.watchOut: Challenge тут — не «кинути виклик» і не «челендж», а прямо спитати когось про щось погане й вимагати пояснень. «Прямо» — directly; straight тут зазвичай не кажуть.

items.pattern: plead ignorance (of sth) · plead – pleaded – pleaded (UK) · fairly formal
items.meaning: say that you didn't know about something, often as an excuse
items.uk: посилатися на незнання, казати, що нічого не знав
items.example: When the parking attendant gave him a ticket, Tom **pleaded ignorance** of the new rules.
more: If you **plead ignorance** every time, people stop believing you.
Half the class **pleaded ignorance** when the teacher asked about the homework.
items.watchOut: Ignorance тут — незнання, а не «неуцтво» чи «ігнорування» (ігнорування — ignoring). Plead тут — «посилатися на щось як виправдання»; plead with sb — «благати когось». Минулий час у британській — pleaded.

items.pattern: complain bitterly (about sth / that…) · also bitterly disappointed / bitterly cold
items.meaning: complain angrily and with strong feeling, because you feel badly treated
items.example: The passengers **complained bitterly** about the four-hour delay.
more: My grandad **complains bitterly** every time the price of bread goes up.
Everyone at the bus stop was **complaining bitterly** about the cold.
items.watchOut: Тут англійська збігається з українською: гірко нарікати — complain bitterly. Але прийменник — about, а не on: complain about the noise. Скаржитися на біль — complain of a pain.

items.pattern: drop a hint / hints (that… / about sth) · drop a heavy / broad hint · take a hint
items.meaning: say something indirectly, hoping the other person will understand what you mean
items.example: I **dropped a hint** that I'd love a new bike for my birthday.
more: She kept **dropping hints** about how tired she was, but the guests stayed until midnight.
Mum **dropped a heavy hint** that the kitchen needed tidying.
items.watchOut: «Кинути натяк» — зазвичай drop a hint, а не throw a hint. Прозорий натяк — a heavy / broad hint. Зрозуміти натяк — take a hint: Can't you take a hint?

items.pattern: (sb's) tone of voice · in a calm / an angry tone of voice · tell sth by / from sb's tone of voice
items.meaning: the way someone's voice sounds, which shows how they feel
items.example: On the phone, Dad's **tone of voice** was so serious that I knew something was wrong.
more: You can say 'no' to a customer, but watch your **tone of voice**.
The receptionist was polite, but her **tone of voice** was cold.
items.watchOut: Тон — tone, а не tune (мелодія) і не note. Часто кажуть in a … tone of voice: She said it in a friendly tone of voice.

items.pattern: make it clear (to sb) that… · make sth clear · make yourself clear
items.meaning: say something so that there is no doubt about what you mean
items.example: Mum **made it clear** that there would be no TV until the homework was done.
more: The landlord **made it clear** to us that pets weren't allowed.
I want to **make** one thing **clear**: I'm not lending you any more money.
items.watchOut: «Дати зрозуміти» — найчастіше make it clear (to sb) that…, з it. Калька give to understand звучить книжно й старомодно. Після make — прикметник clear, а не прислівник clearly.

items.pattern: change the subject (to sth) · quickly / suddenly change the subject
items.meaning: start talking about something different, often to avoid an awkward topic
items.uk: змінити тему (розмови), перевести розмову на інше
items.example: Whenever I ask about his new girlfriend, he **changes the subject**.
more: Let's **change the subject**: this is getting too depressing.
She went red and quickly **changed the subject** to the weather.
items.watchOut: «Змінити тему» — change the subject, а не move the subject. «Перевести розмову на щось» — change the subject to sth.

items.pattern: tell (sb) the truth (about sth) · to tell (you) the truth = honestly
items.meaning: say what really happened or what you really think
items.example: If you broke the vase, just **tell the truth**. I won't be angry.
more: **To tell you the truth**, I didn't enjoy the film at all.
Children usually **tell the truth** if you ask them calmly.
items.watchOut: «Казати правду» — tell the truth, а не say the truth. Так само tell a lie, tell a story, tell a joke. Speak the truth теж буває, але звучить урочисто. To tell (you) the truth на початку речення — «чесно кажучи».

items.pattern: ask (sb) a favour · ask a favour of sb (formal) · compare: do sb a favour
items.meaning: ask someone to help you or do something for you
items.example: Can I **ask you a favour**? Could you feed my cat while I'm away?
more: We **asked** the receptionist **a favour**: could we leave our bags there until the evening?
She **asked** her neighbour **a favour** and borrowed his ladder.
items.watchOut: «Попросити про послугу» — ask sb a favour (або ask sb for a favour), а не ask about a favour. Зробити комусь послугу — do sb a favour: Could you do me a favour? Британське написання — favour, американське — favor.

items.pattern: get into (a) conversation with sb · fall into conversation · informal: get talking to sb
items.meaning: start talking to someone, often someone you don't know, and keep talking
items.example: At the bus stop I **got into conversation** with an old man who'd lived in the town all his life.
more: My son is so shy that he never **gets into conversation** with other kids at the park.
We **got into a conversation** about gardening and missed our stop.
items.watchOut: «Розговоритися з кимось» — get into conversation with sb або fall into conversation with sb, а не enter in conversation (книжне enter into conversation теж правильне). Прийменник — with: with a stranger, а не to a stranger.

items.pattern: join in a / the conversation · join in (sth) · also join the conversation
items.meaning: start taking part in a conversation that other people are already having
items.example: My English got much better once I started **joining in the conversation** at lunch.
more: The new girl stood by the door for ages before she **joined in the conversation**.
Grandad couldn't hear well, so he rarely **joined in the conversation**.
items.watchOut: «Долучитися до розмови» — join in the conversation або join the conversation, без to: не join to the conversation. Join in — включитися в те, що вже відбувається: гру, пісню, розмову.

items.pattern: make polite conversation (with sb) · make conversation · compare: small talk
items.meaning: talk about safe, unimportant things because it's polite, not because you're interested
items.example: At the wedding I had to **make polite conversation** with my cousin's in-laws for an hour.
more: The dentist tried to **make polite conversation** while my mouth was full of cotton wool.
I'm tired of **making polite conversation** at office parties. I just want to go home.
items.watchOut: «Підтримувати розмову з ввічливості» — make (polite) conversation, без артикля, а не do conversation. Lead a conversation — керувати розмовою, спрямовувати її, це інше. Small talk — розмова про погоду й дрібниці.

items.pattern: make an observation (about sth) · an interesting / a funny / a useful observation
items.meaning: say something you have noticed or thought about
items.example: My daughter **made** a funny **observation**: all our neighbours look like their dogs.
more: Can I **make an observation**? You always seem happier after a walk.
The doctor **made** a useful **observation** about my sleeping habits.
items.watchOut: Observation тут — висловлена думка про те, що ти помітив, а не «нагляд» (under observation — під наглядом). Дієслово — make, а не do. «Зробити зауваження» в сенсі «дорікнути» — це радше tell sb off.

items.pattern: address sb politely / formally · address sb as Mr / Mrs / Sir…
items.meaning: speak to someone in a polite way, using the right name or title
items.example: Our new neighbour always **addresses** my grandparents **politely** as Mr and Mrs Green.
more: Even when the customer shouted at her, the shop assistant **addressed** him **politely**.
The new nurse **addresses** all the older patients **politely**, and they love her for it.
items.watchOut: «Звертатися до когось» — address sb, без to: address the guests, а не address to the guests. Turn to sb — це «звернутися по допомогу» або «повернутися до когось». Наголос у дієслові address — на другому складі.

items.pattern: apologise profusely (for sth) · also thank sb profusely
items.meaning: say sorry many times and very strongly
items.uk: без кінця перепрошувати, перепрошувати знову й знову
items.example: The waiter spilt soup on my jacket and **apologised profusely**.
more: Our host **apologised profusely** for the cold room and brought us extra blankets.
When she realised she'd forgotten my birthday, she **apologised profusely** and took me out for dinner.
items.watchOut: Profusely — «рясно, без кінця»; майже завжди з apologise, thank або bleed (bleed profusely — сильно кровоточити). Прийменник — for: apologise for being late. Британське написання — apologise, американське — apologize.

items.pattern: strike up a conversation (with sb) · strike up a friendship · strike – struck – struck
items.meaning: start a conversation with someone, often someone you don't know
items.example: In the post office queue, an old lady **struck up a conversation** with me about the weather.
more: It's easy to **strike up a conversation** with other dog owners in the park.
Two mums **struck up a conversation** at the school gate and became best friends.
items.watchOut: «Зав'язати розмову» — strike up a conversation, а не tie a conversation чи hit up a conversation (hit sb up — американський сленг: «написати комусь, звернутися»). Минулий час — struck.

items.pattern: a lull in the conversation / the traffic · during a lull · an awkward lull
items.meaning: a short time when nobody is talking
items.example: During a **lull in the conversation**, I could hear the clock ticking.
more: There was an awkward **lull in the conversation** when Dad mentioned his ex-wife.
I used a **lull in the conversation** to go and check on the dinner.
items.watchOut: Lull — коротке затишшя після шуму чи активності: a lull in the conversation, a lull in the traffic. Про розмову кажуть з in: a lull in the conversation.

items.pattern: whisper (sth) softly (to sb / in sb's ear) · also speak softly
items.meaning: say something very quietly, using your breath, so that only someone close can hear
items.example: 'The baby's asleep,' she **whispered softly** as we came in.
more: He **whispered softly** in my ear that the film was nearly over.
The nurse **whispered softly** so she wouldn't wake the other patients.
items.watchOut: Softly — тихо, лагідно. Не silently: silently — зовсім беззвучно, а шепіт усе-таки чути. «На вухо» — in / into sb's ear, а не to the ear.

items.pattern: tell (sb) a lie / lies · tell a white lie (a small, kind lie)
items.meaning: say something that you know is not true
items.example: He **told a lie** about where he'd been, and his wife found out the next day.
more: Never **tell lies** to your friends: they always find out.
He's so honest that he can't even **tell a white lie** to be polite.
items.watchOut: «Сказати неправду» — tell a lie, а не say a lie. «Брехати» одним дієсловом — lie (lied, lied): He lied to me. Не плутай із lie (lay, lain) — «лежати».

warmup.uk: Тато виголосив промову на моєму випускному.
warmup.q: Dad ___ a speech at my graduation.
warmup.explain: Виголосити промову — make або give a speech. Say a speech і hold a speech (калька) так не кажуть.
Розповідати анекдоти — tell jokes (або crack jokes). Англійське anecdote — кумедна історія з життя.

warmup.uk: Це не для протоколу, але тренер уже вибрав команду.
warmup.q: This is off the ___, but the coach has already picked the team.
warmup.explain: Не для протоколу — off the record. Protocol — правила, процедура; протокол зборів — the minutes.

warmup.uk: Вона натякнула, що хоче нову сумку.
warmup.q: She ___ a hint that she wanted a new bag.
warmup.explain: Натякнути — drop a hint, хоча українською кажуть «кинути натяк». Make a hint і say a hint — помилки.
Попросити про послугу — ask sb a favour. Do sb a favour — навпаки, зробити комусь послугу.

warmup.uk: Скажи мені правду: ти брав мою машину?
warmup.q: Please ___ me the truth: did you take my car?
warmup.explain: Казати правду — tell (sb) the truth: Tell me the truth. Say the truth — помилка; speak the truth буває, але звучить урочисто, і людину після speak без to не ставлять.

warmup.uk: Бабуся може зав'язати розмову з ким завгодно.
warmup.q: Grandma can ___ up a conversation with anyone.
warmup.explain: Зав'язати розмову — strike up a conversation (strike – struck – struck). Tie — зав'язувати шнурки, а не розмову.

A.q: The best man stood up, ___ a short speech and sat down again.
A.explain: Виголосити промову — make або give a speech. Say a speech і hold a speech так не кажуть.

A.q: Before he borrowed my bike, Jake ___ me his word he'd bring it back by six.
A.explain: Дати слово — give sb your word.

A.q: My parents phoned on the morning of my interview to ___ me luck.
A.explain: Побажати удачі — wish sb luck. Want — «хотіти»; hope з людиною й luck не вживають.

B.q: Who ___ the subject of the broken fence at dinner?
B.explain: Порушити тему — raise the subject. Rise і arise не мають додатка: prices rose, a problem arose.

B.q: Our boss ___ it clear that nobody could take holidays in August.
B.explain: Чітко дати зрозуміти — make it clear (that…).

B.q: When the hotel charged us for the minibar, Dad ___ ignorance: nobody had told him it wasn't free.
B.explain: Plead ignorance — посилатися на незнання. Beg — благати, pray — молитися.

C.q: Come and ___ in the conversation. We're planning the summer holiday.
C.explain: Долучитися до розмови — join in the conversation (або join the conversation).

C.q: The airline ___ profusely for losing our suitcases.
C.explain: Без кінця перепрошувати — apologise profusely. Excuse і forgive — вибачити комусь, а не перепросити самому.

C.q: Grandad sat quietly all evening and then ___ a very clever observation about house prices.

practice.q: At the opening of the new library, the mayor ___ a short speech and cut the ribbon.
My brother has been asked to ___ a speech at our parents' anniversary dinner.
Before the match, the captain made a short ___ to the team in the changing room.
We've only got ten minutes before the train leaves, so please get to the ___.
The letter from the council was three pages long and never really ___ to the point.
My grandmother never wastes words: she always ___ straight to the point.
On long car journeys, Uncle Pete ___ us stories about his time as a sailor.
The old fisherman ___ the children a story about a giant fish.
My aunt told us a ___ about the night she got lost in Venice.
My son ___ me his word that he'd finish his homework before playing football.
Before I lent him the car, he gave me his ___ that he'd drive carefully.
You have my ___: I'll never read your diary again.
Ben ___ jokes all through dinner, and my parents loved him.
Gran is brilliant at ___ jokes: she keeps a straight face until the very end.
Please don't crack ___ about my cooking in front of my mother-in-law.

example.title: The engagement party
example.uk:
На вечірці з нагоди заручин моєї сестри тато виголосив промову. Він кілька разів пожартував, потім перейшов до суті й побажав молодим удачі.

Згодом я розговорився з бабусею її нареченого. Коли в розмові настала пауза, вона тихо прошепотіла: «Можна попросити тебе про послугу? Дізнайся, чи вміє твоя сестра готувати. Мій Том точно не вміє».

Я не хотів казати неправду: у моєї сестри все підгорає. Тож я чітко дав зрозуміти, що куховарство — делікатна тема в нашій родині, і швидко змінив тему. Вона засміялася й натякнула, що Том потай записався на кулінарні курси.
